transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I know the flights are short and safe, but I have this intense, over-the-top fear of getting on a plane that’s now holding me back at work. It's starting to cost me promotions and career advancement because I just can't bring myself to do it.

Is your fear mainly limited to flying, or do you also get the same kind of intense fear in other situations like heights, enclosed spaces, or public places? When you think about boarding a plane, what do you fear most will happen?

Yes, my fear is really just limited to flying, and I've always managed it in the past by just taking road trips instead. When I picture boarding, my biggest fear is that once the cabin door closes, I'll be completely trapped inside while the plane falls out of the sky.

When you have to fly or even think about boarding a plane, do you get sudden physical panic symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, sweating, shaking, or feeling like you might lose control? Do these symptoms happen only around flying?

Yes, absolutely—even just seeing a picture of a plane makes my heart pound, my chest tighten, and my palms sweat. When I actually tried to go to the airport, I froze at the gate, shaking and breathing so fast I had to leave. These intense physical symptoms only happen when it comes to flying, never in any other situation.
